set.descent_text: The gully tops out at a col in the Boott Spur ridge. Skiers click in there; on foot, walk off by way of Hillman's Highway or the Glen Boulder Trail.
set.approach: Begin at the Pinkham Notch Visitor Center on Route 16 and hike up the Tuckerman Ravine Trail as far as the Hermit Lake Shelter. Over the bridge you reach the Sherburne Ski Trail; follow it uphill on the left fork to the foot of the Hillman's Highway slide path. Boott Spur Gully is the long gully on the left side of the rocky buttress that makes up Cathedral Gully's wall. Begin as for Hillman's Highway, then angle left through a brief band of spruce into the gully; the biggest ice bulge comes first, then long sections of snow. The lower slide paths see avalanche, ice and rockfall, so check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Position, ice bulges and top-out from the route page; Hillman's and Glen Boulder walk-offs from the same page.

set.descent_text: The couloir curves left to a top-out on the ridge. Follow the ridge on to Boott Spur's summit, then downclimb Hillman's Highway, or take the Boott Spur Trail down. A marked link trail also drops steeply to the ravine floor near the ranger station, a quick option when wind makes the other ways unappealing.
set.approach: Begin at the Pinkham Notch Visitor Center on Route 16 and hike up the Tuckerman Ravine Trail as far as the Hermit Lake Shelter. Over the bridge you reach the Sherburne Ski Trail; follow it uphill on the left fork to the foot of the Hillman's Highway slide path. Continue up the bushy approach gully near the lower runout of Hillman's Highway, shared with Stovepipe. Where Stovepipe starts at the buttress foot, fork left instead. The approach goes through bushes, snow and bare talus, and then you enter a high-walled couloir. The lower slide paths see avalanche, ice and rockfall, so check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Approach shared with Stovepipe and descent options from the route page.

set.descent_text: The top rolls over almost flat. Mountaineers heading for the summit or coming back should descend the Lion Head Winter Route, or downclimb Right Gully to the ravine floor. A slip here can slide a long way, so be sure of your axe and crampons.
set.approach: Begin at the Pinkham Notch Visitor Center on Route 16 and hike up the Tuckerman Ravine Trail as far as the Hermit Lake Shelter, with the whole ravine in view from there; the trail continues to the floor of the bowl. The Chute is the wide, steep gully right of the obvious Left Gully, with walls closing in at a slight pinch at the bottom. All of Tuckerman's lines lie below big snow slopes, so check the avalanche forecast, and expect skiers above if you descend on foot.

review.notes: Position and descent from route page.

set.descent_text: The route finishes on the Boott Spur summit plateau, a few feet under the high point; a cornice near the top may need working around. To get down, downclimb Hillman's Highway, which is the neighbouring line, or take the Glen Boulder or Boott Spur trail.
set.approach: Begin at the Pinkham Notch Visitor Center on Route 16 and hike up the Tuckerman Ravine Trail as far as the Hermit Lake Shelter. Over the bridge you reach the Sherburne Ski Trail; follow it uphill on the left fork to the foot of the Hillman's Highway slide path. Climb Hillman's Highway roughly one-third of its length, then look for the variation gully on the left side; it leads through a bushy slog to a rock couloir with a choke point. The lower slide paths see avalanche, ice and rockfall, so check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Route and top-out from the route page; walk-offs borrowed from neighbouring Boott Spur lines since both end on the same plateau.

set.approach: Begin at the Pinkham Notch Visitor Center on Route 16 and hike up the Tuckerman Ravine Trail as far as the Hermit Lake Shelter. Over the bridge you reach the Sherburne Ski Trail; follow it uphill on the left fork to the foot of the Hillman's Highway slide path. The Duchess is the big chute right of Hillman's Highway, cutting the big buttress in two. The lower slide paths see avalanche, ice and rockfall, so check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Location only; no top-out or descent is described.

set.descent_text: The final pitch, snow or easy ice, puts you on the upper edge of the ravine. Walk off rightward, or trace the rim right toward Lion Head and descend by the hiking trail.
set.approach: Begin at the Pinkham Notch Visitor Center on Route 16 and hike up the Tuckerman Ravine Trail as far as the Hermit Lake Shelter, with the whole ravine in view from there; the trail continues to the floor of the bowl. The pillars and curtains are high on the center of the headwall, straight up the middle of the ravine. This ice forms early and gets buried as snow fills the ravine. All of Tuckerman's lines lie below big snow slopes, so check the avalanche forecast, and expect skiers above if you descend on foot.

review.notes: Pitch layout and walk-off from the route page.

set.descent_text: The gully ends near the summit of Boott Spur. On skis it is a long run to Pinkham Notch; on foot, descend the way you came. The Boott Spur Trail and Glen Boulder Trail are other ways off, though these may need route finding.
set.approach: Begin at the Pinkham Notch Visitor Center on Route 16 and hike up the Tuckerman Ravine Trail as far as the Hermit Lake Shelter. Over the bridge you reach the Sherburne Ski Trail; follow it uphill on the left fork to the foot of the Hillman's Highway slide path. Follow the wide snow gully uphill. It steepens about halfway with a left and a right split; the left is steeper. The lower slide paths see avalanche, ice and rockfall, so check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Route page; Boott Spur descents also appear on the Cathedral and Stovepipe pages.

set.descent_text: The gully finishes under a headwall that can be steep snow or a large cornice; going left through rocks skirts it. To descend, downclimb or plunge-step the route, or circle the ravine rim to the Alpine Garden. From there Right Gully or Lobster Claw give easy snow back into the ravine, or take the Lion Head Winter Route to the Tuckerman Ravine Trail.
set.approach: Begin at the Pinkham Notch Visitor Center on Route 16 and hike up the Tuckerman Ravine Trail as far as the Hermit Lake Shelter, with the whole ravine in view from there; the trail continues to the floor of the bowl. Left Gully is the left-most gully seen from the floor. Push through the bushes to its base, or go up below the Chute and cut across. Rock walls line it, and it is mostly easy snow. All of Tuckerman's lines lie below big snow slopes, so check the avalanche forecast, and expect skiers above if you descend on foot.

Begin at the Pinkham Notch Visitor Center on Route 16 and hike up the Tuckerman Ravine Trail as far as the Hermit Lake Shelter, with the whole ravine in view from there; the trail continues to the floor of the bowl. Climb Left Gully about halfway, then head left and bushwhack for around a hundred feet until you reach the ice. It shows clearly from the ravine floor and tends to form early in the season, so check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Location from route page; top-out and descent not described, so none written.

set.descent_text: The gully ends at the Alpine Garden, from which you can cross to the summit by the East Snowfields. Descend by Right Gully or Lobster Claw back to the ravine floor, or take the Lion Head Winter Route to the Tuckerman Ravine Trail.
set.approach: Begin at the Pinkham Notch Visitor Center on Route 16 and hike up the Tuckerman Ravine Trail as far as the Hermit Lake Shelter, with the whole ravine in view from there; the trail continues to the floor of the bowl. The route is the narrow gully right of Lobster Claw, reached by a faint runout path through bushes to its base. It does not always fill in. All of Tuckerman's lines lie below big snow slopes, so check the avalanche forecast, and expect skiers above if you descend on foot.

set.descent_text: The steep face eases to low-angle snow with easy access to the East Snowfields. Downclimb the way you came, or take the Lion Head Winter Route to the Tuckerman Ravine Trail; Right Gully and Lobster Claw also make routes down to the ravine. Glide cracks and undermined snow can form late in the season, and the area may be closed then, so follow any signs.
set.approach: Begin at the Pinkham Notch Visitor Center on Route 16 and hike up the Tuckerman Ravine Trail as far as the Hermit Lake Shelter, with the whole ravine in view from there; the trail continues to the floor of the bowl. The Lip is the obvious steep snow face just to the right of the big central icefall on the headwall. All of Tuckerman's lines lie below big snow slopes, so check the avalanche forecast, and expect skiers above if you descend on foot.

set.descent_text: The gully tops out on the Alpine Garden, where you can continue toward the summit. Descend the way you came, or use the Lion Head Winter Route to the Tuckerman Ravine Trail.
set.approach: Begin at the Pinkham Notch Visitor Center on Route 16 and hike up the Tuckerman Ravine Trail as far as the Hermit Lake Shelter, with the whole ravine in view from there; the trail continues to the floor of the bowl. The gully is on the right wall, right of the rock buttress beside Right Gully. A runout gully choked with shrubs leads to the foot of the chute; midway it splits, and the wider right branch is the main line. All of Tuckerman's lines lie below big snow slopes, so check the avalanche forecast, and expect skiers above if you descend on foot.

set.descent_text: The gully reaches the Alpine Garden, with the summit reachable by the East Snowfields or hiking trails. Downclimb the way you came, or use the Lion Head Winter Route; Lobster Claw is another descent. Right Gully is also widely used as a way down from Huntington Ravine.
set.approach: Begin at the Pinkham Notch Visitor Center on Route 16 and hike up the Tuckerman Ravine Trail as far as the Hermit Lake Shelter, with the whole ravine in view from there; the trail continues to the floor of the bowl. Right Gully is the wide gully in the middle of the right wall. Skirt bushes and boulders to enter it; the snow above is straightforward. All of Tuckerman's lines lie below big snow slopes, so check the avalanche forecast, and expect skiers above if you descend on foot.

set.descent_text: After the exit, go up and over and descend easier ground into Hillman's Highway, then come down that gully.
set.approach: Begin at the Pinkham Notch Visitor Center on Route 16 and hike up the Tuckerman Ravine Trail as far as the Hermit Lake Shelter. Over the bridge you reach the Sherburne Ski Trail; follow it uphill on the left fork to the foot of the Hillman's Highway slide path. Side Chute leaves Dodge's Drop about halfway up, on the right, through a steep rock pinch before moderate snow. The lower slide paths see avalanche, ice and rockfall, so check the avalanche forecast.

set.descent_text: Keep pitching the steep snow above the ice until you are comfortable walking. From the top at Lion Head, descend Right Gully or the Lion Head Winter Route.
set.approach: Begin at the Pinkham Notch Visitor Center on Route 16 and hike up the Tuckerman Ravine Trail as far as the Hermit Lake Shelter, with the whole ravine in view from there; the trail continues to the floor of the bowl. The ice lies between The Sluice and Right Gully. Go up the snow gully to the ice, then place a screw to anchor your belayer. All of Tuckerman's lines lie below big snow slopes, so check the avalanche forecast, and expect skiers above if you descend on foot.

set.descent_text: The slot ends in rocks; in early season this is easy scrambling on talus up to the ridge, and in mid to late winter it is usually all snow. The best way down is to downclimb Hillman's Highway. The Boott Spur Trail and Glen Boulder Trail are other options.
set.approach: Begin at the Pinkham Notch Visitor Center on Route 16 and hike up the Tuckerman Ravine Trail as far as the Hermit Lake Shelter. Over the bridge you reach the Sherburne Ski Trail; follow it uphill on the left fork to the foot of the Hillman's Highway slide path. Just above the lower runout of Hillman's Highway, take the first drainage gully on the left, which is bushy. The Stovepipe is the narrow slot on the right side at the base of Cathedral Gully. The lower slide paths see avalanche, ice and rockfall, so check the avalanche forecast.

Begin at the Pinkham Notch Visitor Center on Route 16 and hike up the Tuckerman Ravine Trail as far as the Hermit Lake Shelter. Over the bridge you reach the Sherburne Ski Trail; follow it uphill on the left fork to the foot of the Hillman's Highway slide path. Go about three-quarters of the way up Hillman's Highway to an ice bulge on the left, where the route starts on a low-angle ice ramp. The lower slide paths see avalanche, ice and rockfall, so check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Location from route page; no top-out or descent beyond rock outcrops, so none written.

set.descent_text: Once over the convex roll at the top of the headwall, you cross the Tuckerman Ravine Trail in early season, which makes a fast way down to the ravine floor. If snow has buried the trail, continue up and right to the Alpine Garden and descend Right Gully or the Lion Head Winter Route.
set.approach: Begin at the Pinkham Notch Visitor Center on Route 16 and hike up the Tuckerman Ravine Trail as far as the Hermit Lake Shelter, with the whole ravine in view from there; the trail continues to the floor of the bowl. Look on the right side of the ravine for the large open-book corner with an ice flow running through it. This flow looks different from the stepped ice around it. Walk up to the foot of the corner, where you rope up. All of Tuckerman's lines lie below big snow slopes, so check the avalanche forecast, and expect skiers above if you descend on foot.
